content_html:
Traveling from Lima to Cusco is an adventure in itself. Although the quickest way is to take a plane, traveling this route by land will allow you to discover impressive landscapes, charming towns and unique archaeological sites. Here we show you the perfect itinerary to make this trip an unforgettable experience.

1. First stop: Paracas and the Ballestas Islands

Distance from Lima: 3.5 hours by bus

Your first stop should be Paracas, a coastal destination famous for its beaches and the Paracas National Reserve. From here you can take a tour to Ballestas Islands, known as the “Peruvian Galapagos”, where you will see sea lions, penguins and exotic birds.

Recommended activities:

  • Boat ride through the Ballestas Islands
  • Visit to the Paracas National Reserve
  • Relax on the beaches like Red Beach

2. Adventure in the Huacachina oasis

Distance from Paracas: 1 hour by bus

Huacachina is an oasis in the middle of the desert, ideal for adrenaline lovers. Here you can do sandboarding and tubular rides through the golden dunes. At sunset, the view from the top of the dunes is spectacular.

Recommended activities:

  • Sandboarding and buggy rides
  • Boat ride through the oasis lagoon
  • Wine and pisco tasting in Ica

3. Nazca and its mysterious lines

Distance from Huacachina: 2.5 hours by bus

The Nazca Lines They are one of the greatest archaeological enigmas in the world. They can best be seen from the air on a 30-minute flyby, but there are also ground-based viewpoints.

Recommended activities:

  • Overflight of the Nazca Lines
  • Visit to the María Reiche Museum
  • Explore the Cantalloc Aqueducts

4. Arequipa: The White City

Distance from Nazca: 9 hours by night bus

Arequipa is a colonial jewel surrounded by three volcanoes. Its ashlar architecture and its gastronomy make it worth the stop.

Recommended activities:

  • Tour the Monastery of Saint Catherine
  • Visit the Colca Canyon and see condors in their natural habitat
  • Try the famous stuffed rocoto and Arequipa marinade

5. Puno and Lake Titicaca

Distance from Arequipa: 6 hours by bus

Puno hosts the Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world. Here you can visit the Uros floating islands and the Taquile and Amantani islands, where you will meet local communities with ancestral traditions.

Recommended activities:

  • Boat tour of the Lake Titicaca
  • Live with local families in Amantani
  • Discover the culture of the Uros on their floating islands

6. Cusco: The jewel of the Andes

Distance from Puno: 6 hours by bus or train

Finally, you will arrive in Cusco, the capital of the Inca Empire and the gateway to Machu Picchu. Here you can explore its cobbled streets, Inca temples and markets full of living culture.

Recommended activities:

  • Explore the Historic Center and the Temple of Coricancha
  • Visit the Sacred Valley and its impressive archaeological sites
  • Take the train to Machu Picchu and discover one of the 7 Wonders of the World

Tips for the trip

  • Bring clothing for all types of weather: from the heat of the coast to the Andean cold.
  • Acclimatize in Cusco before doing demanding activities such as trekking.
  • Take advantage of the gastronomy in each destination: ceviche in Lima, pachamanca in Cusco and shrimp chupe in Arequipa.
  • You can buy all this in Cusco itself at a very reasonable price.
